subject: Re: Implementation cadence & schema guardrails for real-time outputs
messages:
From: Asha Reddy <asha@medthread.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Implementation cadence & initial JSON schema (MedThread)

Hi Kimberly / Laura —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our PM and engineering teams reviewed the streaming demo and want to align on an implementation cadence focused on two priorities: (1) getting a minimal real-time payload into production with function/tool calling enabled for prescription lookups, and (2) settling on a constrained JSON schema for structured summaries so we can wire downstream analytics.

I've attached an initial schema (medthread_schema_v1.json) and a proposed 6-week cadence spreadsheet (implementation_cadence_v1.xlsx). High-level asks from our side: 
- Confirm Redwood streaming (server-sent events) support for partial tokens and early structured output emission.
- Define function/toolcall contract for the 'lookup_med_history' tool (inputs/outputs, error handling).
- Gate schema fields for V1 (we want only patient_id, encounter_ts, summary_text, and flags).

Could we get an internal alignment call this week? Prefer 30 minutes on Wednesday PST.

Thanks,
Asha
Asha Reddy
Senior PM, Integrations — MedThread
Attachments: medthread_schema_v1.json (application/json), implementation_cadence_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@medthread.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation cadence & initial JSON schema (MedThread)

Asha —

Appreciate the materials and the clear asks. We're available Wednesday 11:00–11:30 PST for a kickoff alignment. I've looped in Dylan (Solutions) to run the runtime/streaming details and Priyom (Integration Engineer) for schema/validation constraints.

Quick notes ahead of the call:
- Streaming: Redwood supports streaming token flushes and incremental structured emission via our partial-output frames. We will outline two approaches on the call: (a) emit a preliminary JSON envelope as soon as summary_text is stable, or (b) stream tokens and post-process into the constrained schema with a deterministic mapper.
- Tool calling: agree we should define a strict contract for 'lookup_med_history' — Dylan will propose a retry/backoff and error payload shape.
- Schema gating: Priyom can run a quick validation harness against medthread_schema_v1.json and return a reduced shape for V1.

Agenda for Wednesday (11:00 PST, 30m) — please confirm:
1) Quick roles & success criteria (5m)
2) Streaming pattern: partial frames vs final envelope (8m)
3) Toolcall contract and error semantics (8m)
4) Schema gating and rollout plan (4m)
5) Next actions and ownership (5m)

If that works I’ll send a calendar invite with a link and attach the Redwood runtime checklist.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
--
Redwood Inference | kimberly@redwoodinference.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Asha Reddy <asha@medthread.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-21T11:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation cadence & initial JSON schema (MedThread)

Hi all —

Thanks for the note. A couple of runtime specifics to flag before we meet:
- Partial-frame approach: we'll emit a metadata frame containing schema_version, truncated_flag, and token_index. That lets downstream consumers begin processing while token generation completes. We recommend a short-lived prefix cache (60s TTL) for repeated lookups during the same session.
- Toolcall contract: propose this shape for success and error (I'll paste below in the call):
  success: { status: "ok", patient_history: [...], fetched_at: ISO8601 }
  error: { status: "error", code: "NOT_FOUND|TIMEOUT|RATE_LIMIT", message: "...", retry_after: seconds }
- Canary rollout: suggest a 2% traffic bucket on Dedicated with automatic fallback to a baseline model for safety. We can include latency and quality (BLEU/ROUGE or custom accuracy checks) as rollout gates.

I'll bring a sample toolcall payload to the call.

Dylan
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Asha Reddy <asha@medthread.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation cadence & initial JSON schema (MedThread)

Following our Wednesday call — notes and concrete next steps below. (Quoted for context)

On Mon, Jun 21, 2026 at 10:03 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Agenda for Wednesday (11:00 PST, 30m) — please confirm:
> 1) Quick roles & success criteria (5m)
> 2) Streaming pattern: partial frames vs final envelope (8m)
> 3) Toolcall contract and error semantics (8m)
> 4) Schema gating and rollout plan (4m)
> 5) Next actions and ownership (5m)

Notes:
- Agreed approach: emit a "schema_envelope" early with fields {schema_version, patient_id, encounter_ts, partial: true, sequence_id}. Final envelope will include summary_text and flags once generation completes. This lets downstream analytics start ingesting metadata immediately.
- Toolcall contract: standardized HTTP JSON for 'lookup_med_history' with the following minimal interface: inputs = {patient_id, max_records, allow_partial}; outputs = {status, records[], fetched_at, warnings[]}. On error we return codes as Dylan suggested.
- Schema gating: V1 fields locked to {patient_id, encounter_ts, summary_text, flags}. Validation rules: summary_text max 12k chars; flags is enum ["follow_up","med_interaction","critical"]. Priyom will run the schema through our validator and attach a sanitized medthread_schema_v1_reduced.json to the repo.

Next actions (owners & ETA):
- Priyom: produce medthread_schema_v1_reduced.json + validator report (ETA: 2026-06-24 EOD) [attachment planned]
- Dylan: draft toolcall contract and example payloads in the shared Drive (ETA: 2026-06-24)
- Kimberly: send customer-facing cadence and rollout steps + calendar invites for integration windows (ETA: 2026-06-22)
- Asha: confirm downstream consumers and acceptance criteria for analytics (ETA: 2026-06-25)

I ran the schema locally — no breaking issues but removed optional clinical_notes field for V1.

-Priyom
Integration Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Asha Reddy <asha@medthread.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation cadence & initial JSON schema (MedThread)

Thanks team — this is great. Confirming the Wednesday notes and timelines. Two clarifications from MedThread engineering: 
1) For partial envelopes, will the sequence_id be monotonic per encounter? We depend on ordering for incremental analytics.
2) For toolcall rate-limiting, what are the recommended quotas during canary (we expect ~50 TPS for a 2% bucket during peak)?

We'll validate the reduced schema on our side and surface any downstream transforms we need.

Asha

--
Asha Reddy | Senior PM, Integrations — MedThread

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Asha Reddy <asha@medthread.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Implementation cadence & initial JSON schema (MedThread)

Asha —

Short answers and follow-ups: 
- sequence_id: yes, monotonic per encounter and we’ll include an incremental token_index field for replay/resume semantics. We'll add that explicitly to medthread_schema_v1_reduced.json.
- rate limits during canary: recommend you request a temporary quota of 100 TPS to give headroom (we'll throttle to 50 TPS at the routing layer for the 2% bucket and surface 429s with a retry_after header). We will also provide a rate-limit header in responses so your consumers can back off gracefully.

Planned deliverables by EOD: medthread_schema_v1_reduced.json (Priyom), toolcall_contract_v1.md (Dylan), and a short Redwood-runbook.pdf with the canary checklist (Kimberly/Laura). I'll attach the runbook when it's ready and open a Jira ticket to track the rollout gates.

Thanks — we'll sync again once those artifacts are uploaded.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
